title: Census 1951, Rajasthan and Ajmer: District Census Handbook Bikaner, Part II - Primary Census Abstract or Village Directory
villages_named: ladera (serial 54, p.25 -- a second 'Ladera' also exists in Bikaner tehsil, p.~14, so this name has a namesake)
lakhor (as 'Lakhor J36ri', OCR-garbled, serial 31, p.25 -- corresponds to Lakhor Chhoti/Moti but exact qualifier illegible)
bhanabasti (as 'Bhana Basti', p.45, List of Hamlets under Tehsil-2 Lunkaransar)
what_it_contains: THE single most valuable document found: the official pre-1982 (in fact pre-1971 and pre-1961 too) village-by-village census abstract for Lunkaransar tehsil, Bikaner district, from the 1951 Census of India. Lists every revenue village in Tehsil Lunkaransar alphabetically with a serial number, village code, Roman and Devanagari name, area, houses, households, and population by sex, literacy and livelihood class (columns 1-28 spread across several sub-tables per village, pp.16-33 for the whole district covering all 4 tehsils; Lunkaransar tehsil specifically is pp.21-29 approx. for the main directory, plus a 'List of Unpopulated Villages' and 'List of Hamlets' on pp.40-42/45 that include Bhana Basti). OCR text (Adobe Scan-to-PDF, fairly noisy on the Devanagari and on numeric-heavy table cells but usable) confirms 22 of our 37 candidate names existed as named villages/hamlets in Lunkaransar tehsil in 1951, three decades before the 1982-86 MFFR acquisition. File saved locally as dch_bikaner_1951_partII_village_directory.pdf/.txt (47pp, 1.5MB).
how_to_get: Direct download currently blocked from this machine (censusindia.gov.in refuses/SSL-fails here) but the file IS live on the official NADA portal at the URL above (catalog record https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/28566 ). A person with normal internet access should just open that URL and download the PDF. We recovered a full working copy via the Wayback Machine snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20250419033144/https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/28566/download/31748/23629_1951_BIK.pdf and saved it locally -- see files list.

Kumbhaaa ... 54 Ladera ... 31 Lakhor J36ri ... 38 Meusar ... 20 Motasar ... 33 Rampura ... 27 Thoiyan' (OCR text, dch_bikaner_1951_partII_village_directory.txt); hamlet list p.45: 'Tehsi1:-2 LUNKARANSAR ... Bhana Basti'

title: Census 1951, Rajasthan and Ajmer: District Census Handbook Bikaner, Part I - General Description and Census Tables
what_it_contains: Companion volume to the Part II village directory above: narrative description of Bikaner district (4 tehsils: Bikaner, Lunkaransar, Nokha, Kolayat/Magra), history, geography, and tehsil-level (not village-level) summary tables -- e.g. Lunkaransar Tehsil Total population figures. Confirms Lunkaransar tehsil had 3,135 sq. miles and lists it among the district's four tehsils repeatedly (pp.1-40ish). Useful for context/area figures but does NOT itself list individual villages by name -- that is only in Part II above. 135pp OCR text saved locally as dch_bikaner_1951_partI_general.txt (Part I PDF itself was corrupted on re-download and was not kept; the text extraction is preserved and the PDF is re-fetchable from the Wayback URL below).

title: District Census Handbook, Bikaner, Part XIII-A & B (Village & Town Directory + Village & Townwise Primary Census Abstract), Series-18, Rajasthan - Census 1981 (published 1983)
what_it_contains: THE decisive pre-acquisition list. Tehsil 2 Lunkaransar = 171 villages (codes 2/2/1-2/2/171), each with area (ha), population (households) and amenities (Village Directory, PDF pp.155-169: alphabetical list pp.155-157, directory pp.158-169) and full Primary Census Abstract (PDF pp.254-264). Parsed values sum exactly to the printed tehsil totals (623,173 ha; 114,195 persons). ALL 16 test names are present as INHABITED villages in 1981 (none marked uninhabited). 32 entries (29 inhabited + 3 uninhabited 'Rekh') are absent from the 2001 and 2011 lists; their 1981 area totals 135,171 ha = 1,351.7 km2 vs 136,406 ha for 'Mahajan Fieldfiring Range' (2011 code 069202): a 0.9% difference. In 1981 those 29 inhabited villages held 16,018 persons in 2,198 households. The district map (PDF p.14) plots Kanolai with Bas Rampura, Kummana with Bas Dhannasar, Motolai, Mahadeowali Bas Karnisar and Raner with Damolai. Parsed CSV: files/dch_bikaner_1981_lunkaransar_villages.csv.

title: Census of India 2001, Series 09 Rajasthan, District Census Handbook Part A & B, Bikaner (published 2006)
what_it_contains: Supersedes the earlier 'needs-login' entry for this file: it downloads freely. The alphabetical village list (PDF pp.152-158) gives each 2001 village's 2001 AND 1991 location code. The 29 acquired inhabited villages and 3 Rekh villages have NO entries. They are replaced by one village, 'Mahajan Fieldfiring Range' (2001 code 00509900, 'Un-inhabited'). Its 1991 code is Lunkaransar serial 13, so the 1991 census already listed the range as one merged village. Mahadeowali, Kharbara, Gourisar and Gabna @ Lalanwali still exist in 2001, in 'Tehsil Chhatargarh (Part)', so they were NOT acquired. Beermana has no 1991 code. The printed FFR area '13,177.0' ha on p.416 looks like a misprint (2011 gives 1,36,406 ha).
how_to_get: Downloaded: files/dch_bikaner_2001_partAB.pdf (1.6 MB, 526 pp, digital text). censusindia.gov.in works from an ordinary browser. From this sandbox it fails only because the server omits its intermediate TLS certificate ('emSign SSL CA - G1'); fix = download http://repository.emsign.com/certs/emSignSSLCAG1.crt, append it (PEM) to the CA bundle and use curl --cacert <bundle>. NADA JSON search API: https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/api/catalog/search?sk=Bikaner%20Handbook&ps=100&type=document ; file list: https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/<ID>/related-materials
evidence: p.156: '88 Mahajan Fieldfiring Range 00509900 020020002000200013'; p.416: '00509900 Mahajan Fieldfiring Range 13,177.0 ---Un-inhabited---'

title: Census of India 1991, Series 21 Rajasthan, District Census Handbook (Part XII-A & B) - Bikaner volume (NOT digitised on NADA)
villages_named: mahajan fieldfiring range (1991 Lunkaransar serial 13, per 2001 DCH)
what_it_contains: The 1991 Bikaner DCH is NOT in the Census Digital Library: NADA has 18 Rajasthan 1991 DCHs (Ajmer 28660, Bhilwara 28786, Bharatpur 28804, Barmer 28842, Banswara 28856, Churu 28926, Bundi 28985, Ganganagar 29048, Dungarpur 29097, Dhaulpur 29112, Jaisalmer 29189, Kota 29313, Jodhpur 29384, Jhalawar 29393, Nagaur 29402, Sikar 29784, Udaipur 29912, Tonk 29932) but none for Bikaner. From the 2001 DCH's 1991-code column, the 1991 list already shows the range as ONE village (Lunkaransar serial 13) and does not list the acquired villages individually. That makes 1991 of low value for names, but it may carry a footnote on the merger.
how_to_get: Physical copy: Directorate of Census Operations Rajasthan (Jaipur), Census Library at the Office of the Registrar General, 2A Mansingh Road, New Delhi, or NITI Aayog Library (library.niti.gov.in, search 'district census handbook Bikaner'). WorldCat record 982379582 lists holding libraries. Also ask the RGI Census Digital Library to digitise it.

title: Lok Sabha Unstarred Q.2569, 6 Dec 1991: Compensation to Persons Affected due to Acquisition of Land for Field Firing Range in Bikaner Distt. (archive.org mirror of eparlib)
what_it_contains: Q (Manphool Singh): was the Mahajan FFR set up by acquiring the land of 34 villages? A (Defence Minister Sharad Pawar): 'The Mahajan Field Firing Range was established by acquiring the land of 33 villages of Bikaner district'. Full compensation was deposited with the civil authorities; some amounts are held by courts because of disputes.
how_to_get: Free: https://archive.org/download/eparlib.nic.in.41367/10_II_06121991_p92_p92_T90.pdf (OCR text: ..._djvu.txt). Original: https://eparlib.sansad.in/handle/123456789/41367
evidence: 'The Mahajan Fild Firing Range was established by acquiring the land of 33 villages of Bikaner district in Rajasthan.'

title: Lok Sabha Unstarred Q.344, 16 Dec 1996: Acquisition of Land by Defence Forces in Bikaner District (archive.org mirror of eparlib)
what_it_contains: Q (Mahendra Singh Bhati): was all the land of nearly 34 villages in Lunkaransar tehsil acquired for the Mahajan FFR in 1985-86? A: the number is '33 only'. Compensation was paid under the Land Acquisition Act. 4,000 Land Reference cases were filed and some have been dismissed. Rs 89.54 lakh was sanctioned for rehabilitation and given to the District Collector, Bikaner. Other related items on archive.org: eparlib.nic.in.738613 (2011, civilian road near the Army range).
how_to_get: Free: https://archive.org/download/eparlib.nic.in.49395/11_III_16121996_p71_p72_t150.pdf ; archive.org search 'title:(bikaner)' lists more eparlib items
evidence: 'nearly 34 villages in Lunkaran Tehsil ... in the year 1985-86' / '33 only' / '4000 Land Reference cases' / 'Rs. 89.54,000/- for rehabilitation'

title: Primary Census Abstract (Rural) - RAJASTHAN - 1991 (village-level Excel, Census Digital Library/NADA)
villages_named: mahajan field firing range (Lunkaransar 0013, 136,411 ha, pop 0)
what_it_contains: One row per village for all 27 Rajasthan districts (39,810 rows): state/district/tehsil/village codes, name, area (ha), occupied houses, households, population by sex, SC/ST, literates, workers. Bikaner = district 02 (650 villages); Lunkaransar = tehsil 0020 (145 villages, 15 uninhabited, 156,382 rural persons). Village 0013 'MAHAJAN FIELD FIRING RANGE' has 136,411 ha and 0 population. None of the 32 acquired 1981 entries appears separately. Beermana (1981 2/2/80) is missing from the list. This file makes a library visit unnecessary for the 1991 village list.
how_to_get: Free download: https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/43577/download/47283 (1991-PCA-Rural-2100.xlsx, 9.76 MB; censusindia.gov.in needs the emSign SSL CA - G1 intermediate added to a private CA bundle). Local copy: research/leads/files/1991-PCA-Rural-2100_Rajasthan.xlsx; Lunkaransar extract: files/bikaner_lunkaransar_1991_PCA_rural.csv

title: SHRUG v2.2 (Development Data Lab): 1991 Population Census Abstract and 1991 Village Directory, all-India, shrid-level
what_it_contains: 1991 PCA (shrug-pca91-csv.zip, 43 MB) and 1991 Village Directory (shrug-vd91-csv.zip, 25 MB; 100 amenity and land-use columns), aggregated to SHRUG 'shrid' units with no village names. The key pc91r_shrid_key.csv (in shrug-pc-keys-csv.zip) maps 1991 village codes to shrids. Only inhabited villages are linked: in Lunkaransar 130 of 145 villages are linked, and the 15 uninhabited ones, including the Mahajan Field Firing Range, are missing. Useful for 1991 amenities of the surviving villages, not for the range.
how_to_get: Open devdatalab.org/shrug_download, where the links are pre-signed S3 URLs and need no login (list at /shrug_download/data). Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Extracts: research/leads/files/shrug_v2.2_pc91_keys_lunkaransar.csv and shrug_v2.2_pc91_vd_lunkaransar_shrids.csv

title: Directorate of Census Operations Rajasthan, Janganana Bhawan, 6-B Jhalana Doongri, Jaipur-302004 (physical 1991 Bikaner DCH Part XII-A & B)
what_it_contains: Custodian of the Rajasthan census publications. The 1991 Bikaner DCH (Series-21, Part XII-A & B) is not on NADA; 9 of the 27 Rajasthan 1991 DCHs are missing there (Alwar, Bikaner, Chittaurgarh, Jaipur, Jalor, Jhunjhunun, Pali, Sawai Madhopur, Sirohi). The printed book is needed only for Village Directory amenity text or any footnote on the range.
how_to_get: Phone 0141-2708078, e-mail dco-raj.rgi@censusindia.gov.in; ask for a scan of the Lunkaransar pages. Alternative: ORGI, 2/A Man Singh Road, New Delhi-110011 (+91-11-23388132, rgi.rgi@gov.in). Public reading-room rules could not be confirmed online.
evidence: Address from web search results pointing to rajcensus.gov.in/about.html; the site itself returned 502/503 during this check
